newsitem.title: USA: Another Miami commissioner falls foul of law.
newsitem.headline: Another Miami commissioner falls foul of law.

text.p: In the latest blow to Miami's scandal-plagued City Hall, City Commissioner Humberto Hernandez has been indicted in an alleged $8 million mortgage fraud and money-laundering scheme involving luxury condominiums in fashionable neighbourhoods, the U.S. Attorney General's Office said Tuesday.
Hernandez, 35, was one of 13 people named in two indictments unsealed after a Grand Jury's decision Monday.
He surrendered to the Federal Bureau of Investigation Tuesday morning and was clapped into handcuffs.

Hernandez and his associates were alleged to have bought property from each other at inflated prices -- so-called "straw buyers" -- in order to secure huge loans from financial institutions to whom they presented false documents, Assistant U.S. Attorney Caroline Heck told a news briefing.

Hernandez was elected in November to replace Miller Dawkins, now serving a jail sentence after pleading guilty in a corruption and bribery scandal which broke last August. Former city manager Cesar Odio is awaiting sentencing on obstruction of justice charges after corruption charges were dropped against him.

And in May, Port of Miami director Carmen Lunetta quit after the port's finances were revaled to be in mess despite spending on the books for Superbowl tickets, luxury car rentals and campaign contributions to Dade County commissioners.

Hernandez and eight others are charged with engaging in the mortgage fraud, which brought in more than $8 million to secure condominiums in Key Biscayne, Coconut Grove and Brickell Ave. They are also charged with laundering the money.

A second indictment names five people, but not Hernandez, in a related money laundering and Medicare fraud scheme. About $4.5 million from the Medicare scam was passed into the morgtage fraud racket, Heck said.

"Between October 1993 and the present the defendants utilized attorney trust accounts, corporate bank accounts, third party bank accounts under their control, personal bank accounts and off-shore bank accounts in Israel, Curacao and Panama to move and transfer money which derived from a felonious scheme to conduct mortgage fraud and a felonious scheme to conduct Medicare fraud," a statement said.

"Between December 1993 and July 1995 the defendants acted in more than 30 real estate transactions -- variously as buyer, seller, mortgage broker, settlement agent and attorney to the parties -- to conduct real estate transactions in a manner designed to misrepresent to mortgage lenders the nature of the risks of financing real estate transactions."
The "straw buyers" bought properties at inflated prices and funnelled the cash to the sellers, Heck said. She could not say if they defaulted on the loan.
"This is not a theft case. It's a fraud case," she said. "Some defendants were sellers and some were buyers."

The defendants failed to provide deposits and cash to close, submitted false documents including tax returns that were never filed, mistated incomes, submitted fictitious bank statements and false verifications of existing mortgages.
The other defendants included five attorneys, a financial broker, a real estate developer, a mortgage broker, a businessman and a bank employee.
They face up to 30 years in jail on the fraud charges and fines of twice the amount of funds laundered.
